client_situation.text: The RFP is issued by the City of Federal Way, Washington, a city incorporated in February 1990 that changed from a council-manager to a mayor-council form of government in November 2010.

The City is residential and commercial, with an estimated 22,485 people employed within the city limits, and its comprehensive plan calls for a vibrant City Center with mixed-use development and public transportation access.

The City currently runs a legacy environment that it intends to replace with an integrated ERP solution; the RFP presents tables describing the current environment and which solutions are in scope, but the chunk text does not name the specific systems.
The business driver is process improvement: the City expects to improve processes through the new systems and to adopt the best practices offered by the selected Vendor.
The City wants a Vendor with experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
The City is also open to best-of-breed Human Capital Management Vendors, provided their solution can integrate with the selected ERP system.
The City's user base for pricing purposes is 130 named and 85 concurrent Financials users, and 400 FTEs plus 744 W2s for Human Capital Management.

goal.text: The City intends to purchase an integrated ERP solution covering the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document provided with the RFP.

The required Financial modules are General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets and Enterprise Cashiering.
The required Human Capital Management modules are Human Resources, Time and Attendance and Payroll.
The City expects implementation using a phased approach, or another approach recommended by the selected Vendor and approved by the City.
Implementation is scheduled to run from March 2025 through January 2027, following contract negotiations in January 2025 and later.
The proposal must deliver a cover letter executive summary (two pages maximum), a completed Requirements document, Exhibit A pricing, an implementation plan and a support plan.

Pricing must cover software Year 1, implementation services (implementation, data conversion, training, report development, integration, travel, other) and subscription or maintenance for Years 2 through 10.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored by an evaluation committee on Software (30 points), Implementation (25 points), Technology (15 points), Vendor (15 points) and Cost Value (15 points).
The Implementation criterion requires Go Live for all modules in scope by January 1, 2027.

Finalists must present functional and technical product demos to the City following a pre-defined Demo Script, and demo evaluation covers adherence to that script and demonstrated ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements.
Vendor questions are due August 28, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT, and the City posts all questions and answers on its website by September 5, 2024.
Proposals are due September 17, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT by email to Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov, and late submissions will not be considered.
Software missing a significant number of required features and technology preferences may be eliminated from consideration.

Every requirement line item must carry a rating (4 = standard and available, 3 = third-party integrated, 2 = modification with estimated cost, 0 = not available, F = future release with month and year) plus a comment of no more than 100 words, and blank responses may cause the proposal to be rejected as incomplete.
The City may award on the basis of the initial proposal alone, without discussions, and no contract is awarded until approved by City Council.

constraints.text: The proposal must be one electronic PDF of no more than 100 pages (sample contracts excluded) plus one completed Requirements document in MS Word format, with no marketing literature.

The Requirements document is provided as a separate Word document that must be submitted without any change to format, font, numbering or page breaks, with no hyperlinks and no cross-references to other line items.

Pricing must be submitted on the Exhibit A Pricing Summary template, be comprehensive including all taxes and available discounts, and remain valid for 180 days from the response date, with a separate sheet per deployment option (SaaS or on-premises).

The technology overview must cover hosted, on-premises and SaaS architecture options, deployment options, data center locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile hardware and OS options, remote access, integration tools and methodologies, and software update scheduling.

The security overview must cover the security model and standards, security administration including SSO and SAML, multi-factor authentication, and security breach customer communication, response and cost.

References must be submitted on Exhibit B forms with three current and two prior customers of similar size and scope, with preference for Washington State public sector clients, and any contract terminated for convenience or non-performance or legal action with a customer in the past five years must be disclosed.

Sample contract documents must be provided (Statement of Work, Perpetual Software License or SaaS License Agreement, Maintenance or Support Agreements, Service Level Agreements), and any exceptions to the RFP must be documented.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City become the City's property, and no Vendor may mark its entire submittal proprietary.

chunk_summaries.summary: The RFP is issued by the City of Federal Way for Enterprise Resource Planning Software and Implementation Services. Issue date: August 16, 2024. Contact and RFP questions to Thuch Mam at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov. Questions are due August 28, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT. Proposals are due September 17, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT. Vendor responses must be received by the City of Federal Way no later than the indicated date, time and location; late submissions will not be considered and fax submittals are not acceptable.

The City of Federal Way (City) seeks proposals from experienced and qualified Vendors to provide ERP software and services satisfying all of the City's functional and technical requirements. The preferred Vendor shall have experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services; detailed product and service requirements are in Section 3 - Scope of Work and Timeline of this RFP. The City is also open to responses from Vendors providing best of breed solutions for Human Capital Management, which must have the ability to integrate with the selected ERP system; such Vendors complete the Requirements template in Section 6 for the relevant functionality and submit per instructions in Section 5. The submitter is responsible for delivering proposals by the date and time indicated in the RFP; the City accepts no responsibility for lost or misdirected email submittals, is not liable for costs incurred before contract issuance, and all proposal costs are the Vendor's responsibility. All materials submitted become the City's property, are public documents, will not be returned, and submission constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and its exhibits and attachments.

The City began in the late 1800s as a logging settlement; Federal Highway 99 was complete by the 1920s, linking the community to Seattle and Tacoma. The name Federal Way was first used in 1929 when five existing schools consolidated into School District #210 and planned Federal Way High School next to Highway 99. By the end of the 1950s the community had housing areas and a 10-block commercial district with a shopping center and family-oriented theme park; the 1960s brought residential development for Boeing engineers and Weyerhaeuser executives, and SeaTac Mall was built in the mid-1970s. The City incorporated in February 1990 as then Washington's sixth largest city, and in November 2010 citizens changed from a council-manager to a mayor-council form of government. Today the City is residential and commercial, with an estimated 22,485 people employed within the city limits, and its comprehensive plan includes a vibrant City Center with mixed-use development and access to public transportation.

The City intends to purchase an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document provided with this RFP. The City expects to implement a replacement ERP solution using a phased approach, or as recommended by the selected Vendor and approved by the City. The City expects process improvement through implementation of new systems and intends to adopt the best practices offered by the selected Vendor. Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and the system's ability to adapt to user preferences.

The chunk introduces tables that outline the current environment at the City and designate which solutions are considered part of the scope for this project. No specific systems, tables, or scope items are named in the chunk text itself.

The chunk gives the estimated timeline for selection of a Vendor for the City's ERP software and implementation services, and states the City reserves the right to modify or reschedule the timeline as necessary. Dates: Release of Request for Proposals August 16, 2024; Vendor Questions Due August 28, 2024; Vendor Questions Answers Posted September 5, 2024; Proposals Due September 17, 2024; Selection of Finalists October 2024; Software Demos December 2024; Due Diligence Review January 2025; Contract Negotiations January 2025+; Implementation March 2025-January 2027.

An evaluation committee selected by the City will review and score Vendor proposals on five criteria: Software (30 points: breadth of modules offering all modules required, depth of functionality meeting functional and technical requirements); Technology (15 points: adherence to IT strategy for platform, database, accessibility, and integration experience and tools); Vendor (15 points: vendor viability and vision, organizational strength, government entity experience); Cost Value (15 points: software license, subscription, maintenance, implementation services, terms and conditions); and Implementation (25 points: defined and proven implementation methodology, proposed timeline and staffing, Go Live for all modules in scope by January 1, 2027). The City may request clarification of submitted materials, reserves the right to select a Vendor based solely on the information submitted and to award a contract without further discussion, and also reserves the right to conduct discussions with Vendors. Based on evaluation, the City will select Vendors invited to the software demo process, notified via e-mail by the date indicated in Section 3, with notification including a Demo Script document used for on-site demos. The City will conduct pre-demo meetings with finalist Vendors to address questions about logistics of the software demo process and script.

A pre-demo meeting is held to address questions about the logistics of the software demo process and script. Vendors must present functional and technical product demos to the City according to a pre-defined script, and all Vendors must follow that script during their demo process. Demo evaluation criteria include adherence to the script and the ability to successfully demonstrate the product's ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements. The City reserves the right to request additional information, interviews, follow-up demonstrations or other clarification of proposal information to evaluate final Vendors. An evaluation committee will review and evaluate responses in accordance with criteria identified above; clarification of submitted material may be requested during evaluation. The City may award to the successful Vendor based on the initial proposal, or invite them to demo their solution or enter into contract negotiations; no Contract will be awarded until approved by City Council.

Proposals must be prepared simply and economically with concise descriptions of the Vendor's ability to satisfy the City's functional and technical needs, emphasizing completeness and clarity, and must not exceed 100 pages (a Vendor sample contract is excluded from that limit). Ownership of all data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City pursuant to this solicitation belongs to the City; pages considered proprietary must be clearly labeled. Proposals must be emailed to Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov and are due on the date indicated in Section 3 of this RFP; submittals received after the deadline will not be considered, and the official submission time is as marked by Outlook in City staff's email inbox. Responses must include only: one electronic PDF copy of the entire RFP proposal in the order defined in the table, not exceeding 100 total pages (excluding sample contracts), and one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format. Submission of a proposal constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and all exhibits and attachments.

Submitting a proposal constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and all exhibits and attachments. Pre-bid questions may be emailed to the City at thuch.mam@federalwaywa.gov by the due date in Section 3; the City will post all questions and answers to its website by the date indicated in Section 3. No formal prebidders conference will be held. Vendor responses must follow the sections outlined in the RFP; responses deviating from the requested format may be classified as "non-responsive" and disqualified, and marketing literature should not be included.

Section 5 vendor instructions list required proposal sections: 1. Cover Letter (executive summary of proposed software and services for the RFP scope of work, limited to two pages); 2. Requirements (complete the separate Requirements Word document per Section 6 instructions, each requirement rated with a comment on how the function is met, submitted as Section 2 and also in MS Word format without modifying the Word format, each response limited to 100 words); 3. Pricing (complete Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, covering software and implementation services, comprehensive including all taxes and available discounts, valid 180 days from response date, with software cost for the user counts defined in the RFP and one sheet per deployment option if applicable (SaaS or on-premises), implementation services costs required for go live including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training, and license/maintenance cost for Years 1-10); 4. Implementation (implementation methodology overview including sample project plan with phases, tasks and timeline, City resources roles/responsibilities/average time per month, vendor resources roles/responsibilities/average time per month, process improvement strategy, business change management methodology and tools, data conversion methodology, recommended data conversion by module, testing methodology and tools, training methodology and tools, report development); 5. Support (hours, guaranteed response time, resources available, escalation process, baseline vs. premium support, user groups and conferences). Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.

Chunk lists vendor proposal content requirements in Section 5: post go-live tools and services, backup strategy and support, and disaster recovery services (backup, redundancy, location, baseline vs. premium support). Technology overview must cover technical architecture options (hosted, on-premises, SaaS), deployment options, data center locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile hardware and OS options, remote access capabilities, integration tools and methodologies, and software update scheduling. Security overview must cover security model, standards, security administration (SSO, SAML), multi-factor authentication, and security breach customer communication, response and cost. References must use Exhibit B forms with three current and two prior customers similar in size and scope to the City's project, with preference for Washington State Public Sector clients. Vendors must disclose any contract terminated for convenience, non-performance or other reason, or legal action with a customer, in the past five years, including name and address of the contracting party. Sample contract documents requested: Statement of Work, Perpetual Software License or SaaS License Agreement, Maintenance or Support Agreements, Service Level Agreements. Vendors must document any exceptions to the RFP content.

Section 6 gives instructions for completing the ERP Requirements document, which is provided as a separate Word document and will become Section 2 of the vendor's proposal. The requirements list is not comprehensive but contains the key requirements used to evaluate proposals and incorporated into the signed contract. Each item carries a ranking: R for Required, I for Important, N for Nice to Have, or E for Explore; software missing a significant number of required features and technology preferences may be eliminated from consideration. Vendors must provide a rating and a comment for every item, with a brief explanation of how the item is supported; no hyperlinks, no references to another line item, all items addressed in the box provided, and no changes to format, font, numbering or page breaks; blank responses may cause the proposal to be considered incomplete and rejected. Rating scale: 4 = Standard and available (out of the box or configuration included in the proposal); 3 = 3rd party software integrated with the proposed solution (name the application); 2 = Modification (indicate estimated cost); 0 = Not available; F = Future release (indicate anticipated release month and year).

The chunk gives a sample response format for the requirements table, with columns "General" and "Rating and Comment", and a sample row "R" for an Audit Trail requirement: audit trail with user, date, time stamp throughout all modules, with before/after values noted as Important; the sample answer states the system logs all transactions and stamps them with user, date, time and before/after values, and that a report can be generated to review audit history. Respondents must not modify the formatting of each cell. A comment of "Standard Functionality" or similar is not acceptable, and hyperlinks or references to another cell are not allowed; all answers must be placed in their respective box in the table. Each line-item response is limited to 100 words.

Section 7 sets out proposal-process terms: questions, interpretations or clarifications (administrative or technical) about the RFP must be submitted in writing prior to the date indicated in Section 3 – Timeline; all pertinent questions will be answered in writing and conveyed to all proposers through the City's website, and oral statements by any person about the RFP's meaning or intent are unauthorized and invalid. Proposers discovering any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission or other error in the RFP or its attachments must immediately notify the City in writing and request modification or clarification; modifications and clarifications are made by addenda posted on the City's website. A proposer who fails to notify the City before the proposal submission date of an error known, or that reasonably should have been known, bids at their own risk and, if awarded the contract, is not entitled to additional compensation or time for the error or its later correction. The City may modify the RFP, its key action dates or its attachments prior to the proposal submittal date; addenda are numbered consecutively as a suffix to the RFP reference number, proposers are responsible for incorporating all addenda, and failure to acknowledge and incorporate addenda does not relieve the proposer of meeting all terms and conditions of the RFP and subsequent addenda.

Section 7 terms and conditions: addenda will be posted to the City's website. Electronic proposals must be accepted on or before the date and time indicated in Section 3 – Timeline, per Section 5 - Vendor Instructions; late proposals will not be accepted. Proposal development costs are entirely the proposer's responsibility and not chargeable to the City; if the City rejects all proposals it is not liable for proposer costs, damages or loss of anticipated profit. Proposals become the City's property and their information becomes public subject to disclosure laws, and the City reserves the right to use any information or ideas contained in the proposal. Proposers must notify the City in advance of proprietary or confidential material with justification; no vendor may mark its entire submittal proprietary, and the City makes the sole determination of what may be considered proprietary under Public Disclosure laws.

The City retains sole determination of what information may be considered proprietary under its interpretation of Public Disclosure laws; a Vendor cannot mark their entire submittal proprietary. The City may reject any or all proposals, waive immaterial deviations, and may reject proposals that refer to terms and conditions other than the City's as non-responsive. The City may cancel the RFP at any time at its discretion (e.g., project canceled, loss of required funding, or best interest of the City) and has no obligation to make an award or pay proposal preparation costs. Insurance requirements: certification of insurance prior to commencement of any work, an underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage, and the surety must be an admitted surety in the State of Washington. Award, if any, will go to the proposer whose proposal best complies with all RFP requirements and addenda, with evaluation methodology and basis for award described in Section 4 - RFP Evaluation.

Exhibit A – Pricing is a template to be used as Section 3 of the response for all "Required" modules; supporting documents may be included and a separate pricing sheet must be provided for each deployment option. The client is the City of Federal Way, WA, with Financials sized at 130 named users and 85 concurrent users, and Human Capital Management sized at 400 FTEs and 744 W2s. Required Financial Modules listed: General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Project and Grant Accounting (listed twice), Capital Assets, Enterprise Cashiering. Required Human Capital Management Modules: Human Resources, Time and Attendance, Payroll. Pricing structure: Software – Year 1 (with assumptions), Implementation Services (Implementation, Data Conversion, Training, Report Development, Integration, Travel, Other), and Subscription/Maintenance – Years 2-10 (Year 2 through Year 10), each with sub-totals and a Total.

Exhibit B is a "References Current Customers" form with a blank response table for three current customers (Current Customer #1, #2, #3). For each customer the proposer must supply: Name, Employee Count, Population, Contact Name, Contact Telephone and Email, Project Scope, Implementation Duration, Go Live Date, and System Replaced.
